ev.q: As of May 15, 2021, 48.3% of persons identified in CDC’s Vaccine Safety Datalink aged ≥16 years had received ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose
Coverage with ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose was defined as the proportion of persons who received a first dose
By May 15, 2021, 48.3% of persons aged ≥16 years had received ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose, and 38.3% were fully vaccinated.
Coverage with ≥1 dose was lower among non-Hispanic Black (40.7%) and Hispanic persons (41.1%) than among non-Hispanic White persons (54.6%)
Among persons with and without high-risk conditions, Black persons had the lowest ≥1-dose coverage (55.6% and 30.4%, respectively).
Coverage among women was higher than that among men stratified by age, except among those aged ≥75 years
Absolute differences in coverage were calculated using White persons as the reference group
The absolute percentage point difference in coverage between Black and White persons and between Hispanic and White persons increased over the study period
statistical tests were not performed to assess differences between groups.

equity.level_reason: Racial/ethnic coverage disparities are framed, quantified as percentage-point differences from White persons (widening to 14 points) and interpreted; specific social determinants (economic challenges, language barriers, lack of ID, transportation) are named as possible explanations.

level_alternative.reason: The determinants are offered generically in the Discussion, citing another report, as barriers that might exist, not tied to the observed gaps or analyzed.
